title: Synthetic probe gating with differential sampling and budget controls for pin/upgrade events
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an orchestrated probing policy that triggers targeted synthetic evaluations when a catalog model or tenant-pinned model is upgraded or version-locked. The core idea is to gate full-fidelity eval runs using a two-stage approach: lightweight differential probes to detect large regressions, followed by prioritized full probes only when signal and budget thresholds are exceeded. This reduces cost by avoiding full test fanouts for low-risk changes while preserving safety for high-impact transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Create a probe policy schema that supports: per-tenant budget, global budget, prioritized test buckets (smoke, fidelity, long-tail), and sampling strategies (deterministic, randomized, traffic-weighted)
Lightweight differential probes must run within 3 minutes of a pin/upgrade event for catalog and tenant pins and produce a delta score against the golden baseline
If differential probe delta surpasses configured thresholds, schedule prioritized full probes within the release window and notify owners via webhook and console alert
Tenant-level budgets should prevent more than X full probes per 24h (configurable) and allow configurable opt-outs for low-traffic tenants
Expose metrics in Console: probes triggered, probe success/failure rates, cost consumed vs. budget, top failing prompts by weight
End-to-end test harness that simulates catalog pin, tenant pin, and a high-frequency churn scenario with backoff behavior
Documented runbook for false positives, manual re-run, and rollback integration with the pin-promote flow
notes: Motivation: existing eval fanouts for pins cause disproportionate cost spikes for large catalogs and noisy tenants. We need a signal-first gate that balances cost with protection against quality regressions.
Design constraints: must work for both hosted catalog pins (multi-tenant impact) and customer-locked pins (tenant-scoped), and support tenant priority tiers (trial vs enterprise).
Integration points: Pin event webhook -> Eval Orchestrator -> Probe Scheduler -> Eval Runner; Console for visibility and billing for budget throttling.

Risk: differential probes could miss subtle regressions; mitigation is to tune thresholds, expand test coverage for high-risk families, and fall back to conservative default behavior for enterprise tenants.
implementation_plan: Spec schema for probe policy and budgeting (PM + Eng review)
Extend pin event router to include probe policy lookup and early-sample decision
Implement differential probe runner that executes light-weight prompt sets (token-limited, short timeouts) and computes delta metrics
Add budget enforcer service that accounts cost consumption and supports per-tenant throttles and global protective caps
Wire prioritized full-probe fanout with backoff and cancellation semantics; surface decisions to Console
Build Console views and alerts, and add webhook payloads for probe decisions and results
Run staged rollout: internal sandbox -> dogfood tenants -> opt-in enterprise customers -> global default
open_questions: What is the default global budget per pin event before we consider it high-cost? (finance/ops input required)
Should differential probes be model-architecture aware (e.g., more probes for decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) or standardized across models?
What SLA/timeout do we guarantee for differential probes when downstream infra is degraded?
How do we version probe policies so historical pins can reference the policy used at the time of the event?
